solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dog bites back in state of panic

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely, to tail them

indicators.note: back tells us the word for bites is read in reverse

parts.note: nips are small bites

explanation.surface: A dog snaps back at someone in a moment of fright.
explanation.walkthrough: Dog looks like the animal, but it is the verb meaning follow closely.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailspin is a spiralling dive of an aircraft, and figuratively a sudden loss of control or panic.

clue.text: With skill, I stifle one that may be tender-hearted

parts.note: art is skill
to choke is to stifle

explanation.surface: With skill, someone suppresses their kind feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: Tender-hearted sounds like kindly; the vegetable's heart is tender to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: The globe artichoke is prized for its soft, edible heart at the base of its leaves.

clue.text: Cricket sides bagging one run, showing restraint

indicators.note: bagging means capturing, so the sides hold the other letters inside

parts.note: leg and on are both names for the same side of a cricket field, opposite the off side
I is the Roman numeral one
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Cricket teams scoring one run while holding back.
explanation.walkthrough: Leg and on are names of the half of a cricket field behind the batter's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: A leg iron is a shackle placed around a prisoner's ankle to stop them escaping.

clue.text: High official remains boring every year

indicators.note: boring as drilling into: the remains go into the yearly letters

parts.note: PA is per annum, Latin for each year
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A senior official stays dull year after year.
explanation.walkthrough: Boring looks like dull; it means drilling into.
explanation.definitionFit: A pasha was a high-ranking officer or governor in the Ottoman Empire.

clue.text: Veto from President, not acceptable

indicators.note: not means the acceptable word is removed

parts.note: Richard Nixon, 37th US President
on means acceptable, as in that's not on

explanation.surface: A President's veto that is unacceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: To nix something is to reject or forbid it, slang for veto.

clue.text: US roughage cut by British pork pie manufacturer

indicators.note: the British letter cuts into the roughage word, splitting it

parts.note: fiber is the American spelling of fibre, dietary roughage

explanation.surface: A British butcher making pork pies with American high-fibre ingredients.
explanation.walkthrough: Pork pie is Cockney rhyming slang for a lie, so a pork pie manufacturer is a liar.
explanation.definitionFit: In rhyming slang a pork pie is a lie, so someone who makes them is a teller of lies.

clue.text: Long dispute with the very famous advocate of hierarchy

parts.note: a feud is a lasting quarrel
the A-list is the top tier of celebrities

explanation.surface: A long quarrel with celebrities supporting a pecking order.
explanation.definitionFit: A feudalist supports feudalism, a rigidly ranked social order of lords and vassals.

clue.text: Fighting breaks mass defensive structure

indicators.note: the fighting word breaks into the mass word, splitting it

parts.note: bulk means mass
war is fighting

explanation.surface: Combat bursts through a large defensive wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulwark is a rampart or protective wall built for defence.

clue.text: Record provides amusement? Not half!

indicators.note: only half the word is kept, the second half being dropped

parts.note: entertains means provides amusement

explanation.surface: Does a record amuse? Very much so!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'very much', but here it means drop half the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter data is to record it, as entering a figure in a ledger.

clue.text: Male dunking either end of toast in dip

indicators.note: the toast letter is dunked into the word for dip, going inside it

parts.note: to sag is to dip or droop

indicators.note: toast begins and ends with the same letter, so either end gives it

explanation.surface: A man dunking his toast into a dip.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag is an adult male deer, and by extension a man alone, as at a stag party.

clue.text: Religious ceremony allows drinking up several tots?

indicators.note: the two words together take in the next one, as if drinking it

parts.note: Sext is the canonical office said at the sixth hour, around noon
lets means allows

explanation.surface: A church service permits the knocking back of several tots of spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: Tots look like small drinks, but here they are small children.
explanation.definitionFit: Sextuplets are six babies born together, so several tots in one birth.

clue.text: Mark and e.g. Mexican miss complaint

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin
a Latina is a woman or girl of Latin American origin, such as a Mexican

explanation.surface: A young Mexican woman has a blemish and a grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlatina is another name for scarlet fever, and complaint is used for an illness.

clue.text: Rough account penned by the writer then

parts.note: I, the setter referring to themself

indicators.note: penned as in enclosed: the account letters are held inside

parts.note: next means then, afterwards

explanation.surface: A rough draft of an account written by the author afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough estimate is approximate, not precise, which is what inexact means.

clue.text: A kind of whiskey picked up is wrong

indicators.note: picked up as by a microphone, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: rye is a whiskey distilled from rye grain

explanation.surface: Someone mistakes the whiskey they have chosen.
explanation.definitionFit: Awry means amiss or off course, a synonym of wrong.

clue.text: Correspond with Penny, say, not finishing drink

parts.note: a penny is an example of a coin

indicators.note: the drink stops short of its final letter

parts.note: cider is an alcoholic drink made from apples

explanation.surface: Writing letters to a woman called Penny while leaving a drink unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: Penny looks like a pen-friend's name; it is just a coin.
explanation.definitionFit: To coincide is to agree or match up exactly, which is what corresponding things do.

clue.text: Composition in this person's concert put off

parts.note: I'm, short for I am, the setter's own 'this person is'
a prom is a promenade concert, as at the BBC Proms

indicators.note: off as in wrong or awry, so put's letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A piece of music in my concert is postponed.
explanation.walkthrough: Put off looks like postponed; off is only the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An impromptu is a short piece of music in a free, improvised style, a musical composition.

clue.text: Bugging current phone, keeping KGB out of Britain

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

indicators.note: the phone word holds the leftover letter inside it

parts.note: to ring is to phone

indicators.note: the Britain letters are taken out of the agency's initials

parts.note: the Soviet security agency's initials
GB is the abbreviation for Great Britain

explanation.surface: Spies tapping a phone line, with the KGB expelled from Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: The KGB was the Soviet security service; only its first letter survives once Britain's letters go.
explanation.definitionFit: Bugging in the sense of annoying someone; irking means irritating.

clue.text: One tending to issue order is rude man

indicators.note: these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A man rudely gives orders to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Issue order looks like a command; issue means offspring and order is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursemaid looks after children, and issue is an old word for offspring.

clue.text: Get back head of state overthrown by insurrection

indicators.note: overthrown, turned upside down, so in an across clue the letters run backwards

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen as British head of state
a coup is an uprising that seizes power

explanation.surface: A head of state is toppled by an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoup is to recover a loss, regaining money that was spent.

clue.text: Tourist city loves to maintain right state

indicators.note: maintain as in hold, so the loves hold the other pieces

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O, so loves gives two of them
a land is a country or state

explanation.surface: A holiday city's fans keep the state on the right path.
explanation.definitionFit: Orlando, Florida is a city famed as a holiday destination for its theme parks.

clue.text: Playing sitar, strive for this?

indicators.note: playing an instrument; here the letters of sitar are played about with

parts.note: to try is to strive

explanation.surface: A sitar player aims for musical excellence.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: what a sitar player strives for.
explanation.definitionFit: Artistry is creative skill, the quality a musician practising an instrument aims to achieve.

clue.text: Something priests do, given line in contract

parts.note: to shrive is to hear confession and absolve, a priest's task

explanation.surface: Priests are offered a line in a legal agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: Contract looks like a noun, a legal agreement; it is the verb meaning shrink.
explanation.definitionFit: To shrivel is to shrink and wrinkle, as a verb a sense of contract.

clue.text: Blood group felt to lose case for victim of crime

parts.note: AB is one of the human blood groups

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer letters, which are shed

explanation.surface: A blood sample at a crime scene, with felt material losing its covering.
explanation.walkthrough: Felt without its outer letters gives EL.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Abel was murdered by his brother Cain, the first homicide victim.

clue.text: Sheltered area for one on the fiddle?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a shady garden retreat under trees or a trellis
second meaning: someone who bows a violin

explanation.walkthrough: On the fiddle suggests cheating, but it means playing a violin with a bow.
explanation.definitionFit: A bower is a shaded leafy nook, and whimsically a person who draws a bow across strings.

clue.text: Naughty, like a nun who's been expelled?

definitions.text: like a nun who's been expelled?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: no longer part of her religious order

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes order as a religious community a nun belongs to.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means unacceptable behaviour, and literally describes someone removed from a religious order.

clue.text: Group running the game trap criminal boss

parts.note: FA is the Football Association, which governs English football
a gin is a snare or trap for game

explanation.surface: A gang running a racket set a trap for a mob leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Fagin is the leader of the gang of child pickpockets in Dickens's Oliver Twist.

clue.text: Switching around Greek letter, claiming pens etc.

indicators.note: the switching word goes around the Greek letter

parts.note: switching is swapping
nu is the thirteenth letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Swapping Greek letters about while collecting writing pens.
explanation.walkthrough: Pens are female swans. Swan-upping is the yearly round-up of swans on the River Thames, when they are marked to show ownership.
explanation.definitionFit: Swan-upping is the annual Thames census where cygnets and adult swans, pens included, are claimed for their owners.

clue.text: Eminence in East London is indisposed

indicators.note: Cockneys of East London traditionally drop the h at the start of words

parts.note: an eminence is a hill or rise in the ground

explanation.surface: A clergyman of high rank in the East End is unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: Eminence suggests a cardinal's title, but it is raised ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill means unwell or sick, as does indisposed.

clue.text: In which medicine is horrid, by the sound of it

indicators.note: the word for horrid is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: vile means horrid

explanation.surface: A complaint that medicine tastes horrible.
explanation.definitionFit: A vial is a small glass bottle that holds liquid medicine.

clue.text: Walls of unusual room renovated in shiny coat

indicators.note: renovated means done up, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order
the walls of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An oddly shaped room is redone with a glossy layer of paint.
explanation.walkthrough: The walls of unusual are U and L; with ROOM they are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Ormolu is gilded bronze or a gold-coloured alloy used as a decorative gilt finish on furniture.

clue.text: Letter from twin boys round New Year's beginning

indicators.note: the first of the boys goes round the new letter

parts.note: two lads, a pair of boys

indicators.note: the first letter of the word year

explanation.surface: A letter received from twin boys around New Year.
explanation.walkthrough: Letter here means one who lets property, not a written message.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlady lets rooms or property to tenants, so she is a letter in the sense of one who lets.
